Research

DSP uses supervised play to bootstrap robot interaction and planning

The research links human play, autonomous data collection and a world model, while its early hardware evaluation remains provisional.

Robotics Weekly ↗17 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryVideos 2

Learning how to interact

Dexterity from Supervised Play, or DSP, first imitates human object interaction without a specific final task goal. The resulting play policy then collects additional autonomous interaction data to train a world model.

Predicting before acting

Given a goal, the play policy proposes action sequences and the world model predicts their outcomes for model-predictive control. The paper also proposes distilling a policy through play inside the learned model to reduce inference cost.

Hardware conclusions remain provisional

The paper studies object pushing and in-hand reorientation, but its first-version conclusion describes hardware results as provisional and calls for a frozen protocol and uncertainty estimates. Headline gains should therefore not be treated as settled hardware comparisons.
